Kevin Rose's Dark Tips covers Gmail plus-addressing, disposable email via Dodgeit, and encrypted Hushmail, while Brendan Moran recaps the SXSW Interactive Web Awards. notes.title: Gonzo Gizmos, AOTS BBS, LAN Party
notes.summary: This episode features a deep dive into historical internet technology with Simon Field, who explores the mechanics and culture of Bulletin Board Systems (BBS). The show also highlights modern tech trends, reviewing everything from early smartphone cameras to self-balancing Segboards. A major segment involves an interview with Miss Rebecca Love, discussing go-go dancing in China. Finally, Kevin Rose covers industry news via 'The Feed,' reporting on Marvel Comics' new movie funding model.
notes.notable: The detailed historical look at Bulletin Board Systems (BBS) and the demonstration of running old DOS/Amiga games like Dungeon Master is a major nostalgic highlight. The discussion about Miss Rebecca Love's go-go dancing career in China was also notable.

notes.title: Rob Schrab, Star Wars Celebration, Apple's Tiger
notes.summary: This episode covers a mix of tech reviews and pop culture hype. The hosts discuss the latest features of Mac OS X Tiger, including Spotlight and Safari, with expert Scott Michela. They also dive into gaming, reviewing the PSP title Verticube. Much of the show's second half is dedicated to 'The Feed,' where Rob Schraub demonstrates prop-making and puppetry skills for Channel 101, while Kevin Pereira recounts his trip to Star Wars Celebration 3.
notes.notable: The episode features a deep dive into Apple's Mac OS X Tiger update, highlighting new features like Spotlight. It also provides an early look at the gaming potential of PSP titles and includes Rob Schraub demonstrating advanced prop-making techniques for puppetry.

notes.title: Blur Studio, Episode III Video Game, HD Streaming
notes.summary: The episode covered a wide range of topics, starting with an examination of early Windows Longhorn and various internet oddities like Boxed Thoughts and Kittenwar.com. A major segment featured Blur Studio's founders, Tim Miller and Jeff Fowler, discussing their transition from game cinematics to Oscar-nominated short films. The latter half focused heavily on Star Wars, covering fan film awards and a deep dive into the upcoming video game adaptation of Revenge of the Sith. Finally, Kevin Rose reviewed the Buffalo Link Theater, an advanced multimedia DVD player.
notes.notable: The segment discussing MIT's announcement for a Time Travelers convention (May 7th) was noted as a fun historical bit. The appearance and detailed discussion with Blur Studio founders highlighted their meteoric rise in the industry.

notes.title: VideogameDC.com, Hitchiker's Creatures, Chris Gore
notes.summary: The episode features a deep dive into pop culture technology and media, starting with gadget reviews like the Bose and JBL speakers. The segment 'Around the Net' explores how platforms like Flickr are using metadata and tags to categorize information globally. Later segments cover physical media, reviewing DVDs such as Star Trek Enterprise and National Treasure, before moving into tech topics like decentralized BitTorrenting and the benefits of Linux. The episode concludes with a look at animation techniques (Flash) and a segment on eBay auction oddities.
notes.notable: The discussion about 'Azorius' (a trackerless BitTorrent client) was notable for explaining how decentralization allows file sharing to continue even if original trackers fail, addressing a major pain point in P2P networking. The appearance of the Invader Zim box set also served as a fun recommendation.

notes.title: Episode — 2006-01-05
notes.summary: This episode, marking the show's return for 2006, covers a massive amount of pop culture news. The segment begins with coverage of the Consumer Electronics Show (CES), featuring Bill Gates discussing connectivity and Windows Vista. Movie promotion is strong, covering trailers for Mel Gibson's 'Apocalypto' and detailed interviews about Eli Roth's film 'Hostel.' Later segments include a review of new comics by Blair Butler and an interview with Kristana Loken regarding her role in the movie 'Blood Rain.'
notes.notable: The episode covers the first major tech event of 2006, CES. It also features the premiere promotion for Eli Roth's film Hostel, which was based on controversial real-life events.
